Certainly NOT 'fogless.' Quick science lesson... Fog is condensation that forms from the hot, wet air in your shower on the cold (relatively) surface of your mirror. For this to happen there needs to be irregularities in the surface. a 'fogless' mirror has a coating on it to smooth out the surface to prevent this from happening.

This will work for a few showers until residue from the shower starts to build up on the surface, creating irregularities that allow fog to form. If you try to clean off the mirror, you will create scratches in the surface that will also create irregularities, again resulting in fog.

So, this mirror is not magic. Its a good mirror that nevertheless does not violate the laws of physics. Still fogs up. I run the hot shower water over it, warm it up and it stays fog-free long enough for me to shave.
